column2: Satisfied in your own Self by yourself, move in your own Self by yourself; rejoice in the Self alone, and be bodiless and liberated — thus the Upanishad.

The sage named Nidagha asked the revered Ribhu: "Tell me the discrimination between Self and non-Self." Ribhu said: Brahman is the limit of all speech; the teacher is the limit of all thought; the Self of all cause and effect, free of effect and cause;
free of all intentions, Shiva made of all sound; pure consciousness free of all, supreme, made of all bliss;
of the nature of the light of all radiance, made of the bliss of nada; freed from all experience, free of all meditation;
beyond all the parts of nada, this Self, I am, imperishable; free of the distinctions and non-distinctions of discrimination between Self and non-Self and the like;
the Self devoid of peaceful and unpeaceful and the like, of the form of the light within nada; far from the meaning of the great sayings, very far from "I am Brahman";
free of the word "that," devoid of the word "thou," free of the meaning of the sentence; devoid of perishable and imperishable — he is only the light within nada.
Free even of "I am undivided one-savor bliss"; of the nature beyond all — he is only the light within nada.
He who is devoid of the word "Self," free of the meaning of the word Self, devoid even of being-consciousness-bliss, this alone is the eternal Self.
He cannot be pointed to, being unreachable by Vedic sentences; for whom there is nothing outside, nothing inside, nothing at all.
Of whom there is no mark or world — Brahman alone is the Self; no doubt. For whom there is no body, no individual, no elements or elemental things,
no name and form and the like, no object of enjoyment or enjoyer; for whom there is no existent or non-existent, no state, no perishable or imperishable —
with quality or without quality, the Self is even; no doubt. For whom there is no speakable or speaker, no hearing or reflection,
no difference of teacher and disciple and the like, no worlds of gods, gods or demons; where there is no merit or demerit, not even an atom of pure or impure;
where there is no time or non-time, no certainty or doubt; where there is no mantra or non-mantra; knowledge and ignorance do not exist;
no seer, seeing or seen, even slightly, no part; no occasion of "non-Self," no mind of "non-Self,"
nor "non-Self" as world — be certain it does not, does not exist. Because it is void of all intentions and free of all effects,
because it is merely Brahman alone, be certain there is no non-Self; because it is devoid of the three bodies, free of the three times,
because the qualities of the three individuals are absent, because the three afflictions are absent, because it is devoid of the three worlds, by the teaching "all is the Self."
For lack of mind there is nothing to think; for lack of body there is no old age; for lack of feet there is no going; for lack of hands there is no action;
there is no death for lack of people; for lack of intellect there is no pleasure and the like; there is no merit, no purity, no truth, no fear;
no utterance of syllables, no teacher and disciple; where there is no one, there is no second; and not in the second is there oneness.
If there were anything of truth, falsehood could not arise; if there were falsehood, truth would not be tenable.
If you know the auspicious as inauspicious, the auspicious is wished from the inauspicious; if you know fear as non-existence, fear would fall from fearlessness.
If bondage exists, so does liberation; without bondage where is liberation? If there is death, there is birth; without birth there is no death.
If there is "you," there is "I"; if not "you," there is not "I"; if this exists, that exists; without that appearing, this does not.
If it exists, then it does not; if it does not exist, then something does; if there is effect, there is some cause; without effect there is no cause.
If there is duality, then non-duality; without duality there is no pair; if there is the seen, there is the seer; without the seen, no seer.
If inside, then outside is true; without inside there is no outside; if there is fullness, there arises some non-fullness.
Therefore none of this exists anywhere: you, I, these, this; in the truth there is no illustrated, in the unborn no illustrator.
The mind has no place for remembering "I am the supreme Brahman." This world is Brahman alone; you and I are Brahman alone.
I am pure consciousness alone; be certain there is no non-Self. This world does not exist at all, not arisen, nor standing anywhere.
They call the mind the world; it does not exist, it never exists; no world, no mind and the like, no ego, no individual.
No illusion or its effects; illusion does not exist, nor fear; no doer, no action, no hearing, no reflection.
No twofold samadhi, no knower, measure and the like; ignorance too does not exist, nor non-discrimination ever.
No fourfold preliminary, nor threefold relation; no Ganga, no Gaya, no bridge, no being, no other.
No earth, no water, no fire, no wind, no sky anywhere; no gods, no guardians of the quarters, no Vedas, no teacher anywhere.
No far, no atheist, no end, no middle, nothing standing anywhere; no non-duality, no truth of duality, nor this untruth.
No bondage, liberation and the like, existent or non-existent, pleasure and the like; no birth, no goal, no caste, no worldly thing.
All is Brahman does not exist; even "Brahman" does not exist; "consciousness" does not exist; no speech "I am consciousness."
I am Brahman does not exist; "I am eternally pure" is nowhere; whatever is said by speech, thought by mind anywhere,
determined by intellect, does not exist; known by mind, not at all. There is no yogi, no yoga and the like; always all, always not.
No day and night and the like; no bathing, meditation and the like; neither delusion nor non-delusion exists; be certain there is no non-Self.
Veda, scripture, Purana, effect, cause, Lord, world, beings, people, unity — all is false; no doubt.
Bondage, liberation, pleasure, pain, meditation, mind, gods and demons, secondary, primary, supreme and other — all is false; no doubt.
Whatever is said by speech, whatever is imagined by intentions, whatever is thought by mind — all is false; no doubt.
Whatever is determined by intellect, determined anywhere in the mind, extended by scriptures, seen by the eye,
whatever is heard by the ears, and any other existing thing — eye, ear, body are firmly determined as false.
This is what is pointed to; "this" is what is imagined; you, I, that, this, he, and any other existing thing —
whatever is imagined in the world, the confusion of all intention, all superimposition, all secrets, all differences of enjoyment,
and from the distinction of all faults, be certain there is no non-Self. Mine and yours, "of me" and "of you,"
for me, "for you," "by me" and the like — all that is false. Vishnu is the protector, Brahma is the cause of creation,
Rudra of dissolution — be certain all this is false. Bathing, repetition, austerity, oblation, self-study, worship of gods,
mantra, tantra, company of the good, the display of qualities and faults, the existence of the inner instrument and the rise of ignorance,
many crores of universes — be certain all is false. The utterances of all teachers, whatever has been determined by anyone,
whatever is seen in the world, whatever is looked at in the world, whatever exists in the world — be certain all is false.
Whatever is said by any letter, determined by anyone, spoken by anyone, rejoiced in by anyone,
whatever given by anyone, done by anyone, wherever good action, wherever evil action,
whatever you do with truth — be certain all is false. You alone are the Supreme Self; you alone are the supreme teacher.
You alone are of the form of space; you are ever without witness; you alone are all being; you are Brahman; no doubt.
You are free of time, you are time; you are always Brahman, a mass of consciousness; you are of your own nature everywhere; you are a mass of consciousness.

You are truth, you are perfected, you are eternal, you are free, you are liberation, you are joy and nectar; you are god, you are peaceful, you are without disease; you are Brahman, you are full, you are higher than the highest.

You are even, you are being, you are eternal, you are awakened by sayings like "truth"; you are devoid of all limbs, you are ever established; you are contemplated by Brahma, Indra, Rudra and the rest.
You are free of the delusion of all the world; you shine in all beings; you are free of intention everywhere; you are contemplated as the final meaning of all scriptures.
You are everywhere at ease in contentment; you are everywhere free of going and the like; you are everywhere free of aim and the like; you are constantly meditated on by Vishnu and the other gods.
You are of the nature of the form of consciousness; you are mere consciousness, unchecked; you abide in the Self alone; you are void of all, attributeless.
You are bliss, you are the supreme; you are one alone without a second; you are of the form of a mass of consciousness-bliss; you are of fully complete nature.
You are being, you are "thou," you are the knower, you are "he"; you know, you see; you are of the form of being-consciousness-bliss; you are Vasudeva, the lord.
You are immortal, you are all-pervading; you are both moving and unmoving; you are all, you are devoid of all; free of peaceful and unpeaceful.
You are the light of mere being; you are common being; you are of the nature of eternal accomplishment; free of all accomplishments.
You are void of even a trace; free of even an atom; you are free of existence; free of non-existence and the like.
You are devoid of aim and mark, changeless, free of disease; you are inside all nada; free of parts and moments.
You are devoid of Brahma, Vishnu, Ishvara; you behold your own nature; you remain as your own nature; you plunge into the ocean of your own bliss.
In the kingdom of your own Self you are only yourself, free of self-being; you are of the nature of the remaining fullness; you see nothing apart from yourself.
You do not move from your own nature; you expand by your own nature; you are not other than your own nature; be certain that you are I alone.
Whatever this world is, whatever exists in the world, of the form of the seen and the form of seeing, all is like a hare's horn.
Earth, water, fire, wind, space, mind and intellect, ego, light, the world and the orb of the worlds,
destruction and birth, truth, merit, sin, victory and the like, passion, desire, anger, greed, meditation, the object of meditation, the highest quality,
teaching of teacher and disciple and the like, beginning, end, peace, auspiciousness; past, future, present, aim, mark, non-duality;
peace, inquiry, contentment, forms such as enjoyer and enjoyed, the eight-limbed yoga beginning with Yama, of the nature of going and coming,
beginning, middle and inner limb, the graspable, the abandonable, Hari, Shiva, the senses and mind, and the three states likewise,
the twenty-four principles, the fourfold means, same-kind and different-kind, the worlds beginning with Bhu in order,
the conduct of all castes and stages of life, the collections of mantras, tantras and the like, the forms of knowledge and ignorance, all the Vedas, the dull and the non-dull,
the division of bondage and liberation, the forms of knowledge and wisdom, the nature of awakening and non-awakening, the talk of duality and non-duality,
the conclusion of all Vedanta, the determination of the meaning of all scriptures, the existence of many individuals, the decision of one individual and the like,
whatever one meditates on with the mind, whatever one intends anywhere, whatever the intellect determines, whatever one hears from the teacher,
whatever one explains by speech, whatever the teacher says, whatever is contemplated by the senses, whatever is considered separately,
whatever is decided by reasoning by the great who have mastered the Vedas — Shiva dissolves the worlds; Vishnu protects the three worlds;
Brahma creates the worlds, and so on with actions like these; whatever is in the Puranas, whatever is determined in the Vedas,
the sense of all Upanishads — all is like a hare's horn. The intention "I am the body" is called the inner instrument.
The intention "I am the body" is called the great world; the intention "I am the body" is also called bondage.
The intention "I am the body" is called sorrow; the appearance "I am the body" is remembered as hell.
The intention "I am the body" is declared the whole world; the intention "I am the body" is called the knot of the heart.
The knowledge "I am the body" is called ignorance; the knowledge "I am the body" is also non-being.
The intellect "I am the body" is called nescience; the knowledge "I am the body" is called duality.
The intention "I am the body" is the real individual; the knowledge "I am the body" is said to be limited.
The intention "I am the body" is clearly a great sin; the intellect "I am the body" is craving, a disease of faults.

Any intention at all is said to be the threefold affliction. Desire, anger, bondage, all sorrow, the world, fault, the forms of time in many ways — whatever this net of all intentions is, know it, Soma, as mental.
The mind alone is all the world; the mind alone is the great enemy; the mind alone is the world; the mind alone is the three worlds.
The mind alone is great sorrow; the mind alone is old age and the like; the mind alone is time; the mind alone is likewise stain.
